findings.description: The round-1 corrections were added only to `## Overall`. The earlier sections still carry the claims those corrections retract. (a) `## Spec Compliance`, the section gate_logic.check_phase_status parses as `pass`, still says 'No nominal (non-discriminating) coverage found among scenarios 12–15' at line 92. Overall (lines 250-257) says this was false for the scenario-12 CLI case. (b) The header pins validation to commit `5dbc1c7c`, but the scenario-12 test fix landed later in `5d65a958` (it edits skills/tests/audit-choices/test_end_to_end.py). The report records no spot-check showing the new positive assertion discriminates, and the Quality Gates block shows no re-run at HEAD; only the commit message mentions one. (c) The Harness note (lines 12-32) and the D4 bullet (lines 99-102) still say git could not be run against the feature worktree and that `git diff` was not used. Overall says the check was done against both main and the merge base. A reader who stops at the phase section gets the overstated version.
findings.resolution: Correct the claims in `## Spec Compliance` itself rather than only in Overall: drop or qualify the 'no nominal coverage' sentence and name the scenario-12 CLI case. Update the header to the commit actually validated, or add a re-run at 5d65a958 with a mutation showing the new `len(runs) == 1` assertion fails when the run writes nothing. Remove or date-stamp the stale Harness note.

findings.description: The DEGRADED status for `make context-refresh` exists only as prose inside `## Overall`: '**Status of that gate: DEGRADED, not pass.**'. That text does not match gate_logic's `\*\*Status\*\*:\s*degraded` pattern. `## Quality Gates` has no `**Status**:` line at all. So the one check the report admits could not run is invisible to any machine reader, and the report ends in an unqualified '**PASS.**'. The same report also says (line 115) that all tasks.md checkpoints across Phases 1–5 are checked and spot-verified against what shipped. The Phase 5 checkpoint is `[x]`, yet it names context-refresh as a gate that never ran to green. The report does not reconcile that checkbox with its own DEGRADED finding.
findings.resolution: Give `## Quality Gates` a machine-readable `- **Status**: DEGRADED` line naming context-refresh as NOT CHECKED. Qualify Overall as PASS on required phases with one checkpoint gate DEGRADED. Record in the tasks.md note that the Phase 5 checkpoint was ticked with context-refresh unmet, instead of listing it as spot-verified.

findings.description: The report says context-refresh fails for ~30 unrelated changes and is 'unaffected by' this branch, but it never ran the check ('not re-verified here'). A read-only `make context-refresh-check` target exists (Makefile:449), and this branch edits a generated file: `docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md` carries 'Generated by `make decisions` — do not edit manually' and gains two entries on this branch. Reading it, I found those two entries match the only two `architectural:` tags in session-log.md, so drift caused by this branch is unlikely. The report still offers no evidence for 'unaffected'. The contracts/README.md added under the change dir is another producer input whose drift status is unchecked. Separately, session-log.md:102 still reads 'Confirmed all four quality gates green: 366 passed', which contradicts both the corrected count and the DEGRADED status.
findings.resolution: Run `make context-refresh-check` and show that none of the reported drift names a path this branch touches (docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md, the change's contracts/). Otherwise downgrade 'unaffected by it' to 'not verified'. Correct session-log.md:102.

findings.description: D4 checks, independently verified. The four guard files (test_priorities_paths.py, test_retention.py, test_smoke_e2e.py, prioritize-proposals/SKILL.md) do not appear in `git diff origin/main...HEAD` or in `git diff origin/main HEAD`. The characterization test landed in e5889133, before the shared tests (cdbe78ac), the shared module (971944ea) and the migration (1867c3dd), and was never modified afterwards. The subprocess cases really exercise the parents[2] bootstrap from a runtime-shaped copy, with no PYTHONPATH fallback that could mask a broken one. However, the test proves 'nothing observable changed' only for names prioritize-proposals itself produces. It does not prove it in general. The widened RUN_ID_RE, `(?:-(\d+))?`, makes retention count and archive names that main's regex skipped. That covers `<run-id>-N` and also bare `<date>-<digits>` names such as `2026-06-10-1`. Known-unfixed item 5 names only the former. The migration also removed `retention.SKIP_FILENAMES` and the `retention.priorities_paths` module attribute. I found no in-repo users, but D2's 'everything that imports those names keeps working' covers only the listed names. D4's own text says the test pins `latest.*` contents, and it pins only the `latest.*` paths. The report's Overall is honest that the bash-authored body is uncovered, but Spec Compliance says the test 'has three parts as D4 requires' without noting the gap. None of this is reachable from the producer's own output, so low is right.
findings.resolution: In item 5, widen the description to cover any trailing `-<digits>` name, not just `<run-id>-2`. Note the removed `SKIP_FILENAMES` export. In the D4 bullet, state that the characterization test pins producer-shaped inputs and the `latest.*` paths, not `latest.*` contents.

findings.description: The report calls scenario 15 'real' and discriminating on the strength of one mutation, a stray file written at the repo root. But `test_range_form_writes_confined_to_run_directory_and_latest` builds its allowed set from `result.json_path.parent`, the implementation's own answer about where the run went. So the spec clause 'including no file under `openspec/changes/`' is not pinned by this test. An implementation that wrote the pair to `openspec/changes/range:<..>/` and returned that path, while still writing `latest.*` at `openspec/choices/`, would pass it. The clause is covered elsewhere, by scenario-12 tests (test_end_to_end.py lines 476-477 and 525-526, and the always-False routing mutation), so behaviour is guarded. The report's per-scenario claim still overstates what this test shows.
findings.resolution: Either assert inside the scenario-15 test that the run prefix starts with `openspec/choices/` and that no changed key starts with `openspec/changes/`, or qualify the report so that scenario 15's `openspec/changes/` clause is credited to the scenario-12 tests.

findings.description: Known-unfixed items 3 and 4 are recorded honestly, and I confirmed both in the code. Together, though, they amount to more than 'one assertion broader than intended'. Task 5.1, marked `[x]`, explicitly requires the Red Flags case to assert against that specific bullet 'so a mention elsewhere in the file cannot satisfy it'. `_paragraph_containing` returns the whole Red Flags section because the list has no blank lines, and the run-directory check matches the substring "run's" or 'run director' anywhere in that passage. Deleting all three range-form effects from the read-only Red Flags bullet stays green as long as neighbouring bullets mention them. The Read-Only Contract paragraph and Output section cases are unaffected. The other two known-unfixed items (non-atomic `latest.*` pair; `_snapshot` skipping directories, mitigated by TestFailedRangeRunLeavesNoOrphanDirectory and the recursive `range:` name walk in test_end_to_end.py) are correctly rated low.
findings.resolution: Keep the severity at low. The report's tasks.md paragraph should say that task 5.1's paragraph-scoped assertion is unmet for the Red Flags bullet, rather than presenting all tasks as complete.

findings.description: Limits of this review. This session could not run pytest, `uv run`, or `make context-refresh-check` (execution needed approval). The test counts (253 passed / 1 skipped plus 124), the four spot-check mutations, and `openspec validate --strict` were therefore not reproduced. They were checked only for plausibility: the named test classes and functions exist, `is_range_change_id` and `route_output_dir` exist in choices_paths.py, and run_audit.py calls copyfile and then `apply_retention(..., protect=...)` in the order the report describes, each in its own guard. The not-applicable status for Smoke Tests, Security and E2E is correct: work-packages.yaml declares `deployable: false`, every changed path is under skills/, docs/ or openspec/ (non-deployable prefixes in gate_logic), and resolve_required_phases then requires only Spec Compliance.
findings.resolution: Before merge, re-run the three suites and ci_coverage at HEAD (5d65a958) to confirm the recorded counts.
